C-CURSOR-TASK-SENTINEL.Summary: Discharge F90 as out-of-phase hygiene for RM-GOVERNED-PATH P3.1 (lifecycle finish). Stop every guessed task identity on a run event: lint argv token run-commands must not write T-000, and recover / auto-open must not invent T-001. Inherit a plan-declared task that is already in scope; refuse before write when none is. cursor.unknown-task stays a correct checker. Do not write P3 step detail and do not amend the phase board.
C-CURSOR-TASK-SENTINEL.Problem:
F90 (decisions.md): the check ran and was right; the writer is wrong. lint with argv token run-commands records each MustPassCommand through appendCommandRunEvent (src/lint/core.ts:501) and never passes a task. The writer falls back (src/grace-cursor.ts:2977):
options.task, else last loose event task, else the literal T-000.
After a fold, run/ is empty, so the next command-run is T-000. The same fallback fires before any cursor event exists. cursor.unknown-task (src/artifact/grammar.ts:1365) then fires when run.xml names a task the plan does not declare. The position type says known task id only, never a guessed id (A13.2, src/grace-cursor.ts:252). T-000 is a guessed id.
Reproduced at HEAD c3d4b61 from sanctioned commands only, in a temp project that was deleted afterwards. The claim under test is not that T-000 can appear, but that the documented close order lands on cursor.unknown-task.
Documented order (ngrace-execute steps 4, 7, 9): open T-001, terminal T-001, fold, then lint argv tokens assertions final and run-commands. After fold, run.xml still names T-001 and run/ is empty. The command-run file is 3-T-000-command-run.xml. Lint is still green because run.xml has not moved. gate archive refuses no-open-epoch (1 loose event). fold then refuses unterminated range. Terminal of the event's own task T-000 plus fold writes run.xml Task T-000. Lint is then one error, cursor.unknown-task: run.xml names task T-000, which is absent from plan.xml. gate archive permits (run/ empty). cursor regenerate dry-run prints Task T-000, sources epoch=ledger task=ledger state=ledger. The catalog remediation for cursor.unknown-task says regenerate from the ledger and plan; that command re-derives the illegal name.
F90 is right that the transcript overclaimed unreachable. After the poisoned fold, cursor advance with task T-001 and kind terminal (no argv token open-epoch), then fold, leaves run.xml on T-001 and lint at 0 errors; regenerate then follows the last ledger event and stays on T-001. Avoidance also works: after the work fold, a T-001 progress event (again no open-epoch) makes the subsequent command-run inherit T-001. The documented open-epoch form with default from=1 after a prior fold fails with a range hole; that is why the natural reread of "re-open a declared task" does not work. The way back exists and is undocumented. The written order walks into the trap.
T-000 is a well-formed task id (ANCHOR_PATTERNS.task is T- then three digits). A plan may declare it. Generators emit T-001. F90's phrase that the plan can never declare T-000 is false as grammar; it is true of the conventional plan this close produces. The checker fires because the plan does not declare the id, not because the id is reserved.
Writer set that can emit an event whose task the plan does not declare (siblings, not only the run-4 citation):
1. appendCommandRunEvent (src/grace-cursor.ts:2977) invents T-000 when run/ is empty. This is the F90 emitter. 2. recover with argv token fix (src/grace-cursor.ts:616) uses last loose task, else invents T-001. After a T-000 command-run it writes a T-000 opened (inherit, not a new guess). The T-001 fallback is the same A13.2 shape. 3. maybeAutoOpenCoveringAllocation (src/grace-cursor.ts:730) is the same last-or-T-001 guess; fold after a T-000 command-run auto-opens T-000. 4. advanceCursor, pauseCursor, resumeCursor, recordAttempt, and recordVerificationUnavailable accept an operator task that matches T- then three digits and do not check the plan. They can write T-000 if asked. That is operator authorship; the checker is the detection. 5. foldCursor and regenerateCursor write run.xml from the last event or last ledger task. They do not invent a new event id, but they are how T-000 becomes the cursor.unknown-task subject. regenerate of a ledger whose last event is T-000 re-derives T-000.
A repair that changes only line 2977 and leaves the T-001 fallbacks is this repository's repeated defect shape.

Goals.Goal: Never invent a task id on a run event (A13.2). One resolver for appendCommandRunEvent: use a plan-declared task already in scope (last loose event, else run.xml Task, else last folded ledger event), and refuse before write when none of those is a declared id. Delete the literal T-000 fallback.

Apply the same never-guess rule to the T-001 fallbacks at recover argv token fix and maybeAutoOpenCoveringAllocation: inherit the last loose event's task when it exists; refuse rather than invent T-001 when it does not.

Keep cursor.unknown-task as an error for a run.xml Task or EscalatedTask the plan does not declare, including a genuine T-999 and including T-000 when the plan does not declare T-000. Do not exempt a sentinel id.

Make the documented repair honest. Catalog remediation for cursor.unknown-task must not claim that regenerate alone repairs a ledger whose last event is undeclared. Name the sanctioned recovery: advance a declared task with kind terminal (no default open-epoch), then fold.

Document the load-bearing close order in ngrace-execute (canonical and packaged mirror): argv token run-commands after a fold writes loose events; archive requires no-open-epoch; terminal the declared task and fold before archive. Baseline run-commands also requires a declared task already in scope. README.md and examples/ stay unchanged; no user-visible command table or example tree moves.

Constraints.Constraint: Binding: F90; RM-GOVERNED-PATH P3.1 hygiene only. P1 and P2 are complete. P3 is objectives-only and NOT STARTED. This bundle does not write P3 step detail and does not amend the phase board. It exists so lifecycle finish does not inherit a close that plants cursor.unknown-task.
Ceremony tier T1 (module change). status remains draft until the maintainer approves. Do not run gate approve. Do not author plan.xml in this authoring pass (F4).

Chosen repair is F90 candidate (a), which is also brief (a) plus the safe half of brief (b): inherit a declared in-scope task; refuse when none is. In-scope means, in this order: last loose event task if that id is in planTaskIds; else run.xml Task if that id is in planTaskIds; else lastTaskFromLedger if that id is in planTaskIds. Do not pick a plan task by position, by first-task, or by only-task. That would be a guessed id (A13.2) and is not brief (b) as ratified here.

Refuse is invalid-arguments, before any run/ write. The message names the missing declared task and the existing verbs that create one (cursor advance on a declared T-NNN so a loose event exists, or leave run.xml naming a declared task). Do not mention an argv token that this bundle does not add.

Do not add a lint argv token task. Inherit from a declared run.xml Task covers the post-fold close path. First run-commands before any cursor currently invents T-000; after this repair it refuses. That is a protocol change, not a new flag (F18).

cursor.unknown-task, its grammar site, and its severity stay. Do not add T-000 to any exemption set. If a plan declares T-000, that id is a declared task and inherit of it is legal; this bundle does not blacklist the token.

Folded ledgers stay immutable (D9). Recovery of an already-poisoned cursor is in scope as existing verbs, not as a ledger rewrite: cursor advance on a declared task with kind terminal and without default open-epoch, then fold. regenerate of a ledger whose last event is undeclared still re-derives that id; do not teach regenerate to walk backward to the last declared task (that hides history). Update the catalog remediation so it does not claim regenerate alone repairs this state.

Close protocol is in scope. ngrace-execute steps 1, 7, and 9 as written today run argv token run-commands without requiring a declared task in scope and then archive without re-folding. After this repair, step 1 must have a declared task in scope before baseline run-commands; step 7's post-fold run-commands inherit the declared run.xml task when one exists; archive still requires no-open-epoch, so terminal that declared task and fold before gate archive. Do not terminal the event's task when that id is absent from the plan. Do not document default open-epoch after a prior fold: default from=1 leaves a range hole (already noted in src/grace-cursor.test.ts around the C-JOIN-EDIT recovery).

F61: no two adjacent hyphen characters inside any XML comment body. This artifact prefers argv tokens over dashed flags in every comment; element text may name a dashed form but this file avoids that so a later comment cannot regress it.

FIX_SIGNATURE_REPEAT_BUDGET is 2 under exact kind-plus-key equality, so a task may never plan the same signatureKey twice. signatureKey names the property, not the file stem. F90 candidate (c): auto-terminate command-run events so they never become the cursor's current task. Terminal is a judgment (ngrace-execute cursor kinds). A special case for one kind is a fold-semantics change, not a writer repair.
Brief (b) as "pick a task from the plan" (first, last, or only ImplementationPlan child). Plans have no current task. That is a guessed id (A13.2).
A new lint argv token task, a new GraceCommandError code, or a new graph module.

AcceptanceCriteria.AC-INHERIT-DECLARED: After a declared-task epoch is folded so run.xml names that declared id and run/ is empty, lint with argv tokens assertions final, run-commands, and change set writes a kind=command-run event whose task attribute is that declared id, not T-000. Discriminating negative: today's 3-T-000-command-run.xml after a T-001 fold. HEAD today: writes T-000.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-REFUSE-UNSCOPED: lint with argv token run-commands and change set, when run/ is empty and neither run.xml Task nor the last ledger event is a plan-declared task, exits non-zero with invalid-arguments, writes no run/ file, and the message names that no declared task is in scope. Covers the first run-commands before any cursor, and a poisoned run.xml whose Task is undeclared. HEAD today: writes T-000 and lint is green until that id reaches run.xml.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-SIBLING-NO-GUESS: recover argv token fix and maybeAutoOpenCoveringAllocation do not invent T-001 when the last loose event has no task: they refuse before write. When the last loose event has a task, they still inherit that task (including an undeclared one already on disk). HEAD today: the fallback literal is T-001 at src/grace-cursor.ts:616 and :730.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-CHECKER-HOLDS: cursor.unknown-task still fires when run.xml names a task absent from plan.xml, including T-999 and including T-000 when the plan does not declare T-000. Absent run.xml Task stays silent. HEAD today: already true (F45; do not manufacture a red). A change that exempts T-000, or that downgrades the code, fails this criterion.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-REMEDIATE-HONEST: ngrace lint with argv token explain and code cursor.unknown-task no longer tells the operator that regenerate from the ledger and plan is sufficient when the ledger last event is undeclared. Remediation names the sanctioned recovery (advance a declared task, kind terminal, no default open-epoch, then fold). HEAD today: remediation is regenerate from the ledger and plan.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-PROTOCOL-DOCUMENTED: Canonical and packaged ngrace-execute skill text both say: (1) argv token run-commands requires a declared task in scope; (2) after a fold, final run-commands writes loose events and archive requires no-open-epoch, so terminal the declared task and fold before gate archive; (3) do not terminal an undeclared event task to satisfy fold. validate:marketplace stays green. HEAD today: step 7 then step 9 with no re-fold.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-SUITE-AND-LINT: Close-time only, bound to the verdict, not to a task pass (F82). bun test green. bun run ngrace lint with argv token path set to the repo root is 0 errors and 0 warnings. bun run ./scripts/validate-marketplace.ts exits 0. Existing command-run tests that open T-001 before appendCommandRunEvent stay green (they inherit the loose declared task).

AC-CHECKER-HOLDS is HEAD-true and is a stay-true regression, not a red. AC-SUITE-AND-LINT is close-time verdict evidence (F82). Temp-project close sequence from the Problem (fold, run-commands, archive no-open-epoch, declared-task inherit) is the integration shape; do not dogfood this repository's tree as that proof.
